subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — packaging conversion credit & stabilizer carveout (redlines)
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@cloudmetrics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial redline and follow-ups on pricing exhibit

Ben — thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As discussed, attached is CloudMetrics' markup of Exhibit A (pricing schedule) and a short workbook showing the packaging conversion example for our migration year. High level asks:

- We need the minimum floor smoothing (Section 4) clarified for year-1 migration so our GAAP team can forecast.
- We want a one-time conversion credit to offset legacy usage during the onboarding quarter — structure proposed in the workbook.
- Please confirm whether the stabilizer carveout (Section 7.2) applies to reserved-burst credits or only to sustained committed usage.

Laura, tagging you for legal redline reaction / acceptance flags. Ben, can you route this to pricing ops and make sure billing can apply the conversion credit at invoice line-level?

Attachments: CloudMetrics_Redline_v3.docx; Packaging_Conversion_Workbook.xlsx

Thanks — Julia
Julia Park
Sr. Procurement Manager | CloudMetrics Inc.
procurement@cloudmetrics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@cloudmetrics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redline and follow-ups on pricing exhibit

Julia — appreciate the clear markup and workbook. Quick read-through and next steps: 

1) Floor smoothing: we think CloudMetrics is asking us to convert the stated "year-1 minimum" into a pro-rated effective minimum for the migration quarter. That will require an explicit formula in the exhibit so ops can compute the quarterly true-up. Proposed formula in-line: (Annual Minimum * Migration Quarter Days / 365). Does that match your intent?

2) Conversion credit: we can provide a one-time credit applied as a discrete negative invoice line tied to the onboarding invoice. Need legal to weigh in on whether credit should be treated as a rebate (subject to true-up) or a non-recurring billing adjustment.

3) Stabilizer carveout: ops question — if the carveout only applies to committed capacity (reserved), then burst credits would still count toward minimums; if it applies to any credit type, the economics shift materially. Dylan, can you confirm billing system limitation for distinguishing reserved vs burst credits at invoice-level?

Laura — please see Julia's attachment and CloudMetrics' suggested edits. If legal is okay with the pro-rata floor formula and the credit wording (non-recurring invoice adjustment language), we'll push an updated exhibit back to CloudMetrics with redline accepted items.

I'll sync with ops and loop back with a short playbook.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2025 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redline and follow-ups on pricing exhibit

Ben / Dylan — reviewed CloudMetrics' redline and the workbook. High-level legal positions and suggested language below (attached PDF has tracked changes):

1) Floor smoothing formula — ACCEPT with tweak. Replace your proposed parenthetical with explicit exhibit language to avoid ambiguity: "For the Migration Quarter, the Minimum Commitment shall equal (Annual Minimum × (Number of Days in Migration Quarter ÷ 365)), rounded to the nearest whole dollar. The Parties agree that such pro-ration is a one-time adjustment solely for the Migration Quarter and shall not change the Annual Minimum for subsequent periods."

2) One-time conversion credit — COUNTERPROPOSE: we are willing to provide a one-time conversion credit equal to the amount identified in the Packaging_Conversion_Workbook, provided the credit is recorded as a non-recurring invoice adjustment and does not reduce the Annual Minimum used for true-up calculations. Insert clause: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the Conversion Credit shall be a one-time non-recurring invoice adjustment and shall not be considered a credit against or reduction in the Customer's Annual Minimum Commitment."

3) Stabilizer carveout — CLARIFY: recommend we limit the carveout to "Reserved Capacity Credits" and explicitly exclude "Burst or Promotional Credits". Recommended language: "The Stabilizer Carveout applies only to Reserved Capacity Credits as defined in Section 1.4 and does not include Burst Credits, Promotional Credits, or One-Time Adjustments." This preserves expected economics and is defensible to finance.

4) Operational mapping / invoicing: request ops to provide a short playbook entry (2–3 bullets) showing the invoice line tagging and the exponent used for rounding. Also ask Billing to confirm whether the conversion credit can be applied as a negative line that preserves metric mapping to the original SKU for reporting.

I'll attach the tracked PDF (OrderSchedule_ExhibitA_trackchanges.pdf) and the draft redline language as plain text that we can paste into the counter. Let me know if you want a short call with CloudMetrics legal to close language.

Attachments: OrderSchedule_ExhibitA_trackchanges.pdf

— Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com

From: Julia Park <julia.park@cloudmetrics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, CloudMetrics Procurement <procurement@cloudmetrics.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redline and follow-ups on pricing exhibit

Thanks — that plan works for us and the language Laura proposed is clear. Two quick operational asks before we accept the counter: 

- Can Redwood ops confirm the invoice-level negative line will flow into our financial reporting without changing SKU-level consumption numbers (we need the conversion credit to be visible but not to reduce reported usage for compliance reporting)?
- Request a short timeline: if you accept Laura's language we need the executed exhibit by 2025-08-28 to align with our quarter close.

If billing can confirm the negative line treatment, we'll take the counter and sign. Happy to do a 20-minute call with Laura and Dylan if that helps close the loop.

— Julia
Julia Park
Sr. Procurement Manager | CloudMetrics Inc.
procurement@cloudmetrics.com
